metric: Tumour growth rate constant KG (a.k.a. g)
definition: Exponential rate constant of the regrowing/net-growing tumour component, fitted to longitudinal tumour burden under therapy.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Fit N(t)=N0*(exp(-KS*t)+exp(KG*t)-1) to simulated total viable burden N(t)=int_0^R 4*pi*r^2*n(r,t) dr over the on-treatment window; or fit log-linear slope of N(t) after the nadir.
tumor_type: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (PSA as burden surrogate)
direction_of_effect: Higher KG -> shorter OS (Pearson r=-0.72 between log(g) and survival; above-median log(g) mortality HR 5.14, 95% CI 3.10-8.52)
notes: Flagship metric. Direction and functional form validated in patients; the numeric value from a spheroid is not on the patient scale.

metric: Tumour growth rate constant KG - external replication
definition: Same two-phase growth/regression rate constants applied across independent randomised trials.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: As above; KG estimated per simulated combination.
outcome_predicted: Overall survival; discriminated active vs inactive agents
tumor_type: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (8 randomised trials, Project Data Sphere)
direction_of_effect: Higher growth rate g -> worse OS; g separated docetaxel from prednisone/mitoxantrone
notes: Strongest replication of KG/g. Retrospective pooled analysis.

metric: Tumour growth rate constant KG (RECIST-based, immunotherapy)
definition: On-treatment tumour growth rate constant estimated from biexponential fit to sum of longest diameters.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Same fit applied to simulated N(t); use a diameter-like surrogate (spheroid outer radius) if a RECIST analogue is wanted.
outcome_predicted: Overall survival; predicted phase III OS hazard ratio
tumor_type: Non-small cell lung cancer (POPLAR phase II -> OAK phase III, atezolizumab vs docetaxel)
direction_of_effect: Slower KG -> longer OS; model predicted OAK HR 0.73 (95% PI 0.63-0.85) vs 0.73 observed
notes: Notable: PFS was similar between arms while KG separated them - exactly the 'breaks monotonicity with simple response' property we want.

metric: Tumour growth rate constant KG - independent external validation
definition: TGI-OS framework transported to a different drug class and trial.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: As above.
tumor_type: ALK-positive treatment-naive advanced NSCLC (ALEX: alectinib vs crizotinib)
direction_of_effect: Predicted HR 0.612 (95% PI 0.480-0.770) vs 0.625 observed
key_citation: Kassir N 2023, Cancer Chemotherapy and Pharmacology
notes: Confirms KG-OS transportability across drug mechanisms.

metric: Time to tumour growth (TTG)
definition: Model-derived time from treatment start to the point where the fitted tumour-size trajectory turns from net shrinkage to net growth.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Time at which d/dt of simulated N(t) crosses zero from negative to positive (i.e. the nadir time of the fitted biexponential), or first time N(t) exceeds its nadir by a fixed tolerance.
tumor_type: First-line metastatic colorectal cancer (two phase III bevacizumab + chemo trials, Western and Chinese)
direction_of_effect: Longer TTG -> longer OS; TTG was the best of the tested tumour-size metrics and fully captured the bevacizumab effect
key_citation: Claret L 2013, Journal of Clinical Oncology
notes: Best-performing TGI metric in a head-to-head comparison of tumour-size metrics.

metric: Time to growth (replication in a third trial)
definition: As TTG, re-identified as the dominant TGI metric in an independent NSCLC study.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: As above.
tumor_type: NSCLC (GEMSTONE-302, sugemalimab)
direction_of_effect: Longer time-to-growth -> longer OS (most significant TGI metric in the study-specific model)
key_citation: Sheng Y 2023, CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology
notes: Covariates were baseline metastatic-site count and neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio - neither is spheroid-computable.

metric: Depth of response (DpR) / nadir tumour burden
definition: Maximum relative reduction in tumour burden from baseline (the continuous nadir depth, not a RECIST category).
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: DpR = 1 - min_t N(t)/N(0), with N(t) the simulated total viable burden.
outcome_predicted: Progression-free survival, post-progression survival, overall survival
tumor_type: First-line metastatic colorectal cancer (TRIBE phase III, FOLFOXIRI+bev vs FOLFIRI+bev)
direction_of_effect: Deeper response -> longer PFS/PPS/OS; DpR predicted survival as accurately as RECIST response
notes: Continuous, cutoff-free - convenient for a Bayesian-optimisation objective.

metric: Depth of response (DpR) - independent series
definition: Same continuous nadir-depth measure reviewed across mCRC trials.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: As above.
tumor_type: Metastatic colorectal cancer (systematic review of trials 2000-2014)
cohort_size: 10 trials for ETS; 3 of these for DpR
direction_of_effect: Deeper response -> better outcome
key_citation: Heinemann V 2015, European Journal of Cancer
notes: Review-level; use for the ETS/DpR concept, cite Cremolini/Piessevaux for primary effect sizes.

metric: Early tumour shrinkage (ETS) at a fixed early timepoint
definition: Relative decrease in tumour burden at a prespecified early on-treatment assessment (week 6-8 clinically).
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: ETS_sim = 1 - N(t_early)/N(0) at a fixed early simulated time (choose t_early as a fixed fraction of the simulated dosing window).
tumor_type: KRAS wild-type first-line metastatic colorectal cancer (CRYSTAL and OPUS randomised trials, chemo +/- cetuximab)
direction_of_effect: ETS >= 20% vs < 20%: PFS 14.1 vs 7.3 mo (HR 0.32) and OS 30.0 vs 18.6 mo (HR 0.53) in CRYSTAL; PFS 11.9 vs 5.7 mo (HR 0.22) and OS 26.0 vs 15.7 mo (HR 0.43) in OPUS
key_citation: Piessevaux H 2013, Journal of Clinical Oncology
notes: Largest published effect sizes of any metric in this table.

metric: Time to nadir
definition: Time from treatment start to the minimum tumour burden.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: argmin_t N(t) from the simulated burden trajectory.
outcome_predicted: Overall survival (indirectly - determined by the kill and growth rate constants)
tumor_type: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
direction_of_effect: Analytically determined by the regression (d) and growth (g) constants; the authors treat nadir value and time-to-nadir as surrogates for those constants
notes: Report it, but treat it as a derived quantity - it carries no information beyond KS and KG in a two-phase model.

metric: Tumour shrinkage / kill rate constant KS (a.k.a. d)
definition: Exponential rate constant of the drug-sensitive, regressing tumour component.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Second rate constant of the same biexponential fit to simulated N(t).
tumor_type: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
direction_of_effect: log(d) correlated only weakly with survival (r=-0.218) while log(g) correlated strongly (r=-0.72)
notes: IMPORTANT NEGATIVE: kill rate is the metric most naturally read off an in vitro Hill curve, and it is the one that did NOT predict survival. Do not headline KS.

metric: Change in tumour size at a fixed early timepoint (week 8) as an OS covariate
definition: Relative change from baseline in summed tumour size at a fixed early visit, entered in a parametric survival model with baseline covariates.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: As for ETS.
tumor_type: Non-small cell lung cancer (4 registration trials)
direction_of_effect: Greater week-8 shrinkage -> longer survival; ECOG score and baseline tumour size were independent prognostic factors
notes: The two co-predictors (performance status, baseline burden) are not spheroid-derivable - our metric supplies only the tumour-dynamics term.

metric: Baseline tumour burden
definition: Sum of longest diameters of measurable target lesions before treatment.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: N(0) or initial spheroid radius R(0) - but in a simulation this is an input, not a prediction.
outcome_predicted: Overall survival and objective response rate
tumor_type: Advanced melanoma (KEYNOTE-001, pembrolizumab)
direction_of_effect: Below-median baseline size: ORR 44% vs 23% (P<0.001) and OS HR 0.38 (P<0.001); remained independent in multivariate analysis
notes: Set by us, so useless as a discriminating readout - but it must be HELD CONSTANT across combinations or it will confound every other metric.

metric: Residual disease burden after therapy (RCB analogue)
definition: Continuous index of residual tumour after a complete course of therapy.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: N(t_end)/N(0) at the end of the simulated treatment course, plus the surviving-rim thickness (radial extent where n > viability threshold).
tumor_type: Breast cancer after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (two cohorts: T/FAC and FAC)
direction_of_effect: Greater residual burden -> worse DRFS (RCB class in multivariate model HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.70-3.69, P<0.001); minimal residual disease (RCB-I, 17%) behaved like pathologic complete response
key_citation: Symmans WF 2007, Journal of Clinical Oncology
notes: Clinical RCB is a pathologist's index on a resected specimen (tumour bed size, cellularity, node number/size). Nodes are not simulable; the primary-tumour cellularity part maps to our surviving-rim readout by analogy only.

metric: Hypoxic fraction (pO2-histogram based, HP2.5)
definition: Fraction of intratumoural polarographic pO2 readings at or below 2.5 mmHg.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: HF_sim = (int over viable domain of 1[c(r) <= c_thresh] * n(r) * 4*pi*r^2 dr) / (int n(r)*4*pi*r^2 dr), with c_thresh the model equivalent of 2.5 mmHg; report at nadir and time-averaged.
tumor_type: Advanced head and neck cancer treated with primary radiotherapy (7 centres, international)
direction_of_effect: HP2.5 above the population median -> significantly worse OS (P=0.006); most significant factor in a stratified multivariate Cox model; 5-year survival approaches 0% in the most hypoxic tumours
notes: Largest hypoxia-outcome cohort. Our oxygen field is diffusion-only and avascular; the patient measurement includes vascular/acute hypoxia, so the two are analogous but not on a common scale.

metric: Median tumour pO2
definition: Median of intratumoural polarographic oxygen tension readings before treatment.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Median of c(r,t=0) weighted by viable cell density.
tumor_type: Stage IV squamous carcinoma of the head and neck
direction_of_effect: Median pO2 > 10 mmHg vs < 10 mmHg: 12-month DFS 78% vs 22% (P=0.009); relapsing patients averaged 4.1 vs 17.1 mmHg (P=0.007)
key_citation: Brizel DM 1997, International Journal of Radiation Oncology, Biology, Physics
notes: Small cohort but a clean, often-cited effect.

metric: Tumour hypoxia (median pO2 < 10 mmHg) and malignant progression
definition: Dichotomised pretreatment oxygenation status.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: As median pO2 above.
outcome_predicted: Disease-free and overall survival; occult local spread
tumor_type: Locally advanced carcinoma of the uterine cervix (FIGO Ib bulky-IVb)
direction_of_effect: Hypoxic tumours (50% of patients) had significantly worse DFS and OS; oxygenation and FIGO stage were the leading independent prognostic factors; failures were predominantly locoregional
notes: Oxygenation was independent of clinical stage and tumour size - evidence that a hypoxia readout adds information beyond size. No DOI registered for this 1996 Cancer Research paper (PMID 8813149).

metric: Hypoxic subvolume (FMISO-PET hypoxic volume, HV)
definition: Volume of tumour with tracer tissue-to-blood ratio above 1.2 on 18F-fluoromisonidazole PET before radiotherapy.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Absolute hypoxic volume = int over 1[c(r) <= c_thresh] * 4*pi*r^2 dr (an absolute volume, not a fraction).
outcome_predicted: Time to progression and overall survival
tumor_type: Glioblastoma multiforme, pre-radiotherapy
direction_of_effect: Greater hypoxic volume or greater maximum T/B ratio -> shorter TTP and shorter survival (P<=0.001 by Kaplan-Meier; P<0.002 univariate)
notes: Both an absolute hypoxic volume and a normalised fraction are outcome-associated - report both, since spheroid size varies across simulated conditions.

metric: Immunohistochemical hypoxia score (pimonidazole-positive area)
definition: Fraction of tumour section area positive for the 2-nitroimidazole hypoxia marker pimonidazole, with vascular density.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: No direct analogue: requires an administered marker and stained tissue. The closest surrogate is the hypoxic-fraction readout above.
tumor_type: Head and neck carcinoma (biopsies, ARCON-eligible)
direction_of_effect: Hypoxic tumours or tumours with low vascularity had significantly lower locoregional control
notes: Vascular density is not simulable at all. No DOI registered (PMID 12460928).

metric: Hypoxia gene-expression classifier (15-gene)
definition: Transcriptional signature classifying tumours as hypoxic or not.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: NOT computable - requires transcriptomic measurement.
outcome_predicted: Locoregional control and survival; also predicted benefit from hypoxic modification
tumor_type: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (randomised nimorazole vs placebo with radiotherapy)
direction_of_effect: Classifier-hypoxic tumours had significantly worse outcome, which was restored to the non-hypoxic level by adding hypoxic modification
notes: Cite as evidence that hypoxia is causally actionable in patients, NOT as a metric we can compute.

metric: Histologic coagulative tumour necrosis
definition: Presence of coagulative necrosis on pathological review of the resected tumour.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Necrotic fraction/core radius is directly computable, but the histologic entity has partly different causes (vascular collapse, not pure diffusion limitation).
tumor_type: Renal cell carcinoma (Mayo Clinic Nephrectomy Registry, 1970-2002)
direction_of_effect: Necrosis present vs absent: death-from-RCC risk ratio 5.27 (95% CI 4.56-6.09, P<0.001) in clear cell and 4.20 (95% CI 1.65-10.68) in chromophobe; not significant in papillary (1.49, 95% CI 0.81-2.74, P=0.199)
notes: Largest cohort in this table. Tumour-type dependent - not a universal prognosticator, and RCC is not in NCI-ALMANAC's panel.

metric: Pretreatment intrinsic radiosensitivity (SF2)
definition: Surviving fraction of tumour cells at 2 Gy measured ex vivo before treatment.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Not applicable (no radiation in the model), but methodologically the closest precedent for an in vitro potency measure predicting patient outcome.
outcome_predicted: Overall survival, local control, metastasis-free survival
tumor_type: Stage I-III carcinoma of the uterine cervix, radiotherapy
direction_of_effect: SF2 below median vs above: 5-year survival 81% vs 51%; SF2 was the strongest variable in multivariate analysis, independent of stage, grade, age and tumour diameter
key_citation: West CML 1997, British Journal of Cancer
notes: Included deliberately: it is the strongest published precedent that a purely in vitro cell-survival parameter can be independently prognostic in patients. Use it in the Discussion, not as a readout.

metric: Tumour volume doubling time (TVDT)
definition: Time for untreated tumour volume to double, from serial imaging.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: TVDT = ln(2)/lambda from a log-linear fit to untreated simulated N(t); in practice this is set by our Gompertz/logistic calibration, so it is an input.
tumor_type: Small (<=5 cm) untreated hepatocellular carcinoma in cirrhosis
direction_of_effect: Doubling time ranged 27-606 days (median 172); growth pattern and doubling time entered multivariate analysis of survival
notes: Natural-history cohort, not a treatment-effect metric. Keep TVDT fixed across combinations.

metric: Invasion velocity v = 2*sqrt(D*rho)
definition: Asymptotic radial expansion speed of a travelling wave in the Fisher-KPP equation, with D the cell diffusivity and rho the net proliferation rate.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Direct from the model's own D and rho parameters; also measurable as the slope dR/dt of the simulated outer radius at a fixed density threshold.
outcome_predicted: Overall survival (via the underlying rho and D estimates)
tumor_type: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, serial pretreatment MRI
direction_of_effect: Higher model-derived proliferation and invasion rates -> worse prognosis, significant after controlling for age and Karnofsky performance status
notes: TIER A ONLY FOR IMAGING-CALIBRATED GLIOMA. D and rho were fitted to each patient's own serial MRI (T1Gd and T2 radii). In our setup D is a fixed physical constant of the medium, so v cannot vary with drug combination unless the drug changes rho - the metric is largely degenerate for our use case.

metric: Velocity of radial expansion (v) measured on paired pretreatment scans
definition: Radial growth speed computed from two pretreatment MRI volumes with no intervening treatment.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: dR/dt on the simulated density-threshold radius.
outcome_predicted: Survival relative to model-predicted untreated survival
tumor_type: Glioblastoma imaged twice before radiotherapy
cohort_size: small proof-of-principle series (single-digit to low-double-digit patients)
direction_of_effect: Wide inter-patient spread in v, D and rho; about half the patients survived as predicted without treatment (radioresistant) and about half survived up to roughly twice as long
notes: Explicitly a proof of principle; small n. Cite for the method, not for an effect size.

metric: Invasiveness ratio rho/D
definition: Ratio of net proliferation rate to cell diffusivity; high values are 'nodular', low values 'diffuse'.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Direct from model parameters (rho/D). In our model both are inputs, so this is a fixed constant across drug combinations.
outcome_predicted: Overall survival benefit from gross total resection (treatment-effect modification, not prognosis per se)
tumor_type: Contrast-enhancing gliomas, routine pretreatment MRI
direction_of_effect: Nodular (high rho/D) tumours gained significantly from gross total resection (P=0.00142; median survival benefit over eight months, ~80% improvement vs subtotal resection) while diffuse tumours gained nothing (P=0.532)
notes: DO NOT CLAIM. Largest and cleanest rho/D result, but (i) it predicts benefit from SURGERY, not chemotherapy, (ii) it needs patient imaging calibration, and (iii) rho/D is a fixed input in our model. Cite as motivation for spatial modelling generally.

metric: Days Gained (model-based response metric)
definition: Difference between the model-predicted untreated tumour trajectory and the observed post-treatment trajectory, expressed in days of growth delay.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Simulated analogue: time shift between treated and untreated N(t) curves at a matched burden threshold - a growth-delay measure.
outcome_predicted: Time to recurrence and overall survival; distinguished true progression from pseudoprogression
tumor_type: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, first post-radiotherapy MRI
direction_of_effect: Higher Days Gained -> longer time to recurrence and longer OS
notes: The CONCEPT (model-predicted-untreated minus treated, as a time shift) transfers cleanly to a spheroid and is arguably our best-motivated spatial readout. The patient VALIDATION is imaging-calibrated glioma under radiotherapy - do not claim our version is validated.

metric: Model-derived proliferation rate rho linked to hypoxic burden
definition: Patient-specific net proliferation rate from MRI-calibrated Fisher-KPP, correlated with PET hypoxia.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: rho is a model input; the hypoxia coupling (hypoxic burden rising with proliferation) is emergent and checkable in our model.
outcome_predicted: Association between growth kinetics and hypoxic burden (mechanistic link, not a survival endpoint in this paper)
tumor_type: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma with FMISO-PET and serial MRI
direction_of_effect: More aggressive model kinetics associated with greater hypoxic burden
notes: Useful as a face-validity check on our coupled model: our simulations should reproduce the direction of this association. n=11, and no survival endpoint here.

metric: Radiotherapy-response parameter from patient-specific PDE model
definition: Model-estimated radiation efficacy fitted per patient by matching predicted and observed post-treatment imaging.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Analogous fitting could be done for a drug term, but our drug term is prescribed from the Hill curve, not fitted to patient data.
tumor_type: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma treated with radiotherapy
direction_of_effect: Model-predicted response varied widely across patients and tracked observed outcome
key_citation: Rockne R 2010, Physics in Medicine and Biology
notes: n=9. Method paper. Requires patient imaging to calibrate.

metric: Drug penetration depth (distance to half perivascular concentration)
definition: Distance over which drug concentration falls to half its value at the source boundary.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: From the simulated drug field: L_half = R_outer - r at which C(r) = 0.5*C(R_outer); report per drug and time-averaged over dosing.
outcome_predicted: Mechanism of chemoresistance (spatial escape of viable cells from drug exposure)
tumor_type: Murine 16C and EMT6 tumours and human PC-3 xenografts (doxorubicin)
direction_of_effect: Doxorubicin concentration decayed exponentially with distance from vessels, halving over ~40-50 um, while hypoxic regions lay 90-140 um away; many viable cells saw no detectable drug
notes: Quantitative anchor for our penetration length scale. Xenograft, not patient outcome.

metric: Penetration-limited drug exposure in multicell layers
definition: Depth-resolved drug concentration through a ~200 um multicellular layer grown on a permeable support.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Same as penetration depth, in slab rather than spherical geometry.
outcome_predicted: Resistance of solid tumours to chemotherapy (mechanism)
tumor_type: EMT-6 mouse mammary and MGH-U1 human bladder multicell layers
direction_of_effect: Cisplatin, etoposide, gemcitabine, paclitaxel and vinblastine all penetrated slowly relative to the support membrane alone
notes: Directly relevant: five of these drugs are in the ALMANAC panel. No DOI registered (PMID 11895922).

metric: Taxane penetration limit (~100 um)
definition: Depth of paclitaxel/docetaxel penetration into tumour tissue and multilayered cell culture.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: As penetration depth, per drug, using drug-specific D.
outcome_predicted: Reduced drug effect (S-phase depletion) in cells distant from vasculature
tumor_type: HCT-116 xenografts and multilayered cell culture
direction_of_effect: Little drug beyond ~100 um; paclitaxel penetrated up to 2-fold better than docetaxel; up to 75% reduction in S-phase cells near vessels but not far from them
notes: Gives drug-to-drug differences in penetration - the mechanism by which our model can reorder combinations relative to in vitro potency.

metric: Packing-density / adhesion dependence of penetration
definition: Penetration through multicellular layers as a function of cell packing density and cadherin-catenin adhesion.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Enters the model as the tortuosity/effective-D scaling with cell density n(r); a sensitivity axis rather than a readout.
outcome_predicted: Therapeutic efficacy in the model system
tumor_type: Colon carcinoma sublines (epithelioid vs round; alpha-E-catenin differences)
direction_of_effect: Paclitaxel, doxorubicin, methotrexate and 5-fluorouracil all penetrated significantly better through loosely packed than tightly packed layers
notes: Justifies making effective drug diffusivity density-dependent; also names 4 ALMANAC drugs.

metric: Methotrexate tissue-penetration determinants
definition: Factors governing penetration of a small-molecule antifolate through solid tissue.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Same penetration machinery; supports drug-specific diffusion/consumption parameters.
tumor_type: Multicell layer model
direction_of_effect: Penetration limited and modifiable by tissue properties
key_citation: Cowan DSM 2001, International Journal of Cancer

metric: Multicellular resistance not seen in monolayer ('in vivo only' resistance)
definition: Resistance to alkylating agents that appears in three-dimensional/in vivo context but not in monolayer culture.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Emergent in our model: the same Hill curve yields lower kill in 3D than in a well-mixed setting.
tumor_type: Murine tumour models, alkylating agents
direction_of_effect: Resistance conferred by mechanisms operative only in vivo
notes: Historic anchor for the whole premise that in vitro potency overstates 3D efficacy.

metric: Review-level synthesis of penetration barriers
definition: Overview of transport limitations that keep drugs from reaching all tumour cells.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Conceptual framing for the drug PDE.
tumor_type: Solid tumours generally
direction_of_effect: Limited penetration is a general and modifiable cause of resistance
notes: Review - use for framing only, never as a source of an effect size.

metric: Hypoxia- and necrosis-associated chemoresistance in spheroids
definition: Chemosensitivity as a function of spheroid size and the presence of hypoxic and necrotic zones.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Directly reproduced: kill per unit dose falls as hypoxic fraction and necrotic core grow with spheroid radius.
tumor_type: Colorectal cancer cell spheroids (size series)
direction_of_effect: Spheroids containing both hypoxic and necrotic zones most closely resembled in vivo expression profiles and were the most 5-FU-resistant
notes: The single most on-point experimental validation for our model's core mechanism, and 5-FU is in ALMANAC.

metric: Oxygen diffusion limit / viable rim thickness (~150-200 um)
definition: Distance from an oxygen source beyond which cells cannot remain viable, seen histologically as a viable rim around a necrotic core.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Viable rim thickness = R_outer - r_necrotic where r_necrotic is where c(r) falls below the necrosis threshold; a direct model output.
outcome_predicted: Motivates hypoxic radioresistance in human tumours (original observation)
tumor_type: Human lung cancer histology
direction_of_effect: Necrotic centres appear once tumour cords exceed roughly twice the oxygen diffusion distance, implying a viable rim of order 100-200 um
key_citation: Thomlinson RH 1955, British Journal of Cancer
notes: Foundational, but a histological/mechanistic observation - not an outcome-validated metric.

metric: Oxygen enhancement of radiation response (why hypoxia matters mechanistically)
definition: Dependence of radiobiological damage on dissolved oxygen concentration at irradiation.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Not applicable (no radiation term in our model).
tumor_type: Radiobiology, general
direction_of_effect: Oxygen concentration at irradiation determines biological effect
key_citation: Gray LH 1953, The British Journal of Radiology
notes: Cite only to explain why hypoxia was historically measured; irrelevant to a chemotherapy-only model.

metric: Oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and spheroid growth
definition: Mechanistic link from cellular oxygen consumption and doubling time to the sigmoidal spheroid growth curve.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Our model's own oxygen reaction-diffusion equation; OCR is a calibratable parameter with published values.
outcome_predicted: Growth-curve shape and oxygen distribution (model validity, not patient outcome)
tumor_type: Multiple cell lines, spheroids
direction_of_effect: Derived growth curves from doubling time and OCR; recovered OCR values consistent with independent measurement, and inferred gemcitabine-induced OCR change
notes: Best source for calibrating our oxygen parameters, and evidence that drug effects on OCR are inferable from spheroid growth.

metric: Spheroid oxygen consumption and diffusion coefficients (measured)
definition: Experimental determination of OCR and oxygen diffusivity in multicellular spheroids.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Parameter source for the oxygen PDE.
tumor_type: Multicellular spheroids
direction_of_effect: Provides the measured constants that set the oxygen penetration depth
notes: Cite for parameter provenance.

metric: Spheroid internal structure from mathematical modelling (necrotic/quiescent/proliferating zones)
definition: Model-based decomposition of a spheroid into proliferating rim, quiescent zone and necrotic core, fitted to spheroid data.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Direct: zone radii and zonal cell counts from n(r,t) and c(r,t).
tumor_type: Tumour spheroids (in vitro, model-fitted)
direction_of_effect: Zonal structure and its dynamics are recoverable from growth and staining data
notes: Methodological precedent for exactly the zone-partition readouts we propose.

metric: Time to regrowth after treatment stops
definition: Time from end of therapy until tumour burden returns to a reference level (e.g. baseline or nadir + x%).
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: First simulated time after dosing ends at which N(t) >= N(0) (or nadir*(1+x)); with a post-treatment simulation window.
outcome_predicted: Proxy for time-to-progression; NOT itself validated in patients
tumor_type: n/a
direction_of_effect: Mechanistically monotone with residual burden and net growth rate
notes: Closely related to the validated TTG and Days Gained metrics but not itself an outcome-validated endpoint. Report as an engineering readout, label tier C.

metric: Surviving-rim cellularity / residual viable shell geometry
definition: Amount and radial location of viable tumour cells surviving therapy.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: int over the viable shell of n(r,t_end)*4*pi*r^2 dr, plus rim thickness and its inner/outer radii.
outcome_predicted: Mechanistic driver of regrowth; the primary-tumour cellularity component of clinical residual-burden indices
tumor_type: n/a (analogous to breast RCB cellularity term, validated only as part of the full pathological index)
direction_of_effect: More surviving rim -> faster regrowth in the model
key_citation: Symmans WF 2007, Journal of Clinical Oncology
notes: The clinical index it resembles (RCB) is Tier A, but RCB includes nodal terms we cannot simulate; our version is a mechanistic analogue only.

metric: Tumour growth inhibition (TGI) in xenografts as a translation bridge
definition: Percent inhibition of xenograft tumour growth relative to control, simulated at clinically relevant human exposures.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Analogous: percent reduction in simulated burden at a matched drug exposure.
tumor_type: 8 molecularly targeted and cytotoxic agents with known clinical outcome
direction_of_effect: Significant correlation (r=0.91, P=0.0008) between simulated xenograft TGI at human pharmacokinetics and clinical response, but NOT when TGI at the mouse maximum tolerated dose was used
notes: Crucial caveat: the correlation held only after correcting for human exposure. Our model has no PK - so this supports the approach only if we are explicit that we are comparing at matched exposure, not matched dose.

metric: Preclinical tumour-growth-inhibition PK-PD model (Simeoni)
definition: Minimal PK-PD model of tumour growth under drug, yielding a drug-potency parameter k2 transferable across compounds.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Our kill term is the spatial generalisation of this; the fitted potency parameter is the non-spatial analogue.
outcome_predicted: Antitumour activity in xenografts; basis for predicting active human doses
tumor_type: Xenograft studies, multiple anticancer agents
direction_of_effect: Model captured xenograft growth kinetics and yielded a transferable potency index
notes: Methodological ancestor of our kill term. Companion paper extends it to predicting active human doses.

metric: Preclinical-to-clinical active-dose prediction
definition: Use of the preclinical PK-PD potency parameter to predict active doses in humans.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: n/a - requires PK.
tumor_type: Anticancer agents, animal-to-human translation
direction_of_effect: Preclinical potency estimates supported prediction of clinically active doses
key_citation: Rocchetti M 2007, European Journal of Cancer
notes: Requires pharmacokinetics; we have none. Cite as the limitation we are not addressing.

metric: Choice of growth law (Gompertz vs logistic vs exponential)

metric: Hypoxia-targeting fails when patients are unselected (tirapazamine)
definition: Randomised addition of a hypoxia-activated cytotoxin to chemoradiotherapy without hypoxia-based selection.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: n/a - a cautionary clinical result.
tumor_type: Stage III/IV squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (TROG 02.02 HeadSTART, phase III)
direction_of_effect: 2-year OS 65.7% (cisplatin) vs 66.2% (tirapazamine + cisplatin); no difference in failure-free survival, time to locoregional failure or quality of life
key_citation: Rischin D 2010, Journal of Clinical Oncology
notes: ESSENTIAL CAUTION: hypoxia is prognostic, but a hypoxia-directed intervention in unselected patients did not improve survival. A model that predicts hypoxia-modulated kill is not thereby predicting patient benefit.

metric: Organoid drug response predicts patient response (ex vivo, drug-specific)
definition: Ex vivo drug sensitivity of patient-derived organoids compared with the same patient's clinical response.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Conceptually our target: an ex vivo 3D readout mapped to clinical response. Our model is a simulation of a 3D system, one step further removed.
outcome_predicted: Clinical response to the same agent
tumor_type: Metastatic colorectal cancer (prospective)
direction_of_effect: The organoid test identified non-responders to irinotecan-based therapy in >80% of patients without misclassifying benefiters, but FAILED to predict response to 5-fluorouracil plus oxaliplatin
notes: The drug-specific failure is the key lesson: 3D ex vivo predictiveness is agent-dependent, not general.

metric: Organoid recapitulation of patient responses across agents
definition: Comparison of organoid, PDX and patient responses in phase 1/2 trial participants.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: As above.
tumor_type: Metastatic colorectal and gastroesophageal cancer (phase 1/2 trial patients)
direction_of_effect: Organoid responses recapitulated patient responses in the clinic
notes: Best-case evidence for 3D ex vivo predictiveness; still not a simulation, and heavily pretreated patients.

metric: Tumour growth rate constant KG - second prostate replication
definition: Growth and regression rate constants from serial PSA under five successive treatment regimens.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: Same biexponential fit to simulated burden.
tumor_type: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (five intramural NCI phase II trials)
direction_of_effect: Growth rate constant g correlated with survival and was superior to PSA doubling time; g fell ~10-fold across a decade of successively more effective regimens (log g from 10^-2.08 for thalidomide to 10^-3.17 for combination therapy)
notes: Also the source of an important exception: in the vaccine arm, survival benefit appeared WITHOUT a corresponding change in g - so KG is not a universal surrogate across mechanisms.

metric: Change in tumour size at week 7 as an OS predictor (original TGI-OS framework)
definition: Model-estimated relative change in tumour size at a fixed early time, with baseline tumour size, in a parametric survival model.
formula_from_spheroid_rd_model: As for ETS, at a fixed early simulated time.
tumor_type: Metastatic colorectal cancer (capecitabine phase II n=34; historical fluorouracil phase III n=252; survival model n=245; validated by simulating an independent phase III)
cohort_size: 245 for the survival model; 923-patient class of phase III trials simulated
direction_of_effect: Greater week-7 shrinkage and smaller baseline tumour size -> longer survival (both P<0.00001); predicted median OS 431 days (90% PI 362-514) vs 401 observed
key_citation: Claret L 2009, Journal of Clinical Oncology
notes: The founding paper of the TGI-OS approach; establishes that early tumour-dynamics metrics plus baseline burden suffice to predict a phase III survival distribution.
